title: Kimberly Guilfoyle denies allegations of misconduct as she resigns as US ambassador to Greece – live
text: 12.36 EDT Kimberly Guilfoyle denies allegations of misconduct in statement announcing resignation Kimberly Guilfoyle , who White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia said earlier was asked to resign as the US ambassador to Greece, denied allegations of engaging in misconduct in a statement announcing her resignation. “These allegations are false, and I intend to vigorously defend my name, my reputation, and my integrity. I have dedicated my professional life to fighting for justice, standing up for what is right, and defending the values that make America exceptional,” Guilfoyle said in a post shared to X . “I will not allow false accusations to define my decades of public service,” her statement continued. Despite the call for her resignation earlier today, Guilfoyle remained steadfast in her support of President Trump. “My gratitude and respect for President Trump and Secretary Rubio remain unwavering. I am proud of what we accomplished together, and I will always be a loyal supporter of President Trump and his mission to Make America Great Again.”

Поднявшаяся буря разметала корабли осаждавших, город был спасён. Отсюда и название — Покров. text: ‼️ 🇷🇺 🫡 Промышленный бум в России ▪️ Под руководством президента в последние годы в России открылось множество крупных промышленных объектов. Новые заводы появились в самых разных отраслях — от добычи и переработки сырья до машиностроения, энергетики, стройматериалов и пищевой промышленности. ▪️ Сырьё и нефтегазохимия Одним из наиболее масштабных проектов стала Удоканская горно-металлургическая компания в Забайкальском крае. Предприятие выпускает медный концентрат и относится к числу крупнейших промышленных проектов, запущенных в стране за последние годы. В Иркутской области заработал Тайшетский алюминиевый завод, выпускающий первичный алюминий. В нефтегазохимии заметным событием стал запуск «ЗапСибНефтехима» в Тюменской области, ориентированного на производство полимеров и другой нефтехимической продукции. Отдельно стоит выделить Амурский газоперерабатывающий завод. Он перерабатывает природный газ и производит гелий, а также широкую фракцию лёгких углеводородов — сырьё для дальнейшей химической переработки. ▪️ Машиностроение и сельхозтехника В машиностроении одним из главных событий стало открытие в 2024 году тракторного завода «Ростсельмаша» в Ростове-на-Дону. Это первый в постсо

title: Ukraine is littered with landmines on a scale last seen in Vietnam. How can they be removed?
text: A Halo Trust deminer working in a field. Photograph: Julia Kochetova/The Guardian Faced with deadlier threats, demining groups are coming up with new ways of working using drones and AI By Amy Hawkins in Kharkiv region. Photographs by Julia Kochetova Wed 14 Oct 2026 00.00 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google C rouched over on her hands and knees in a field of weeds, Olena Kabanova is digging into the ground. With a shovel and a steady hand, the 58-year-old digs out a neat square around the spot where a mine detector has sensed a suspicious object. Four years ago, this field in eastern Ukraine was occupied by Russian soldiers. Now back under Ukrainian control, it is littered with landmines. Civilians such as Kabanova are trying to make the land usable again. Landmines are a scourge of conflict zones. Littered across contested territory, they leave land unusable for years after a war has ended. Removing them is an expensive and dangerous job. And the use of long-range drones in Ukraine, which is often described as the most mine-contaminated country in the world, is increasing the scale of the problem. title: Trump repeats false claim about Iran’s nuclear weapons program at Alaska rally – as it happened
text: 21.10 EDT Trump repeats false claim Iran was 'two weeks away from having a nuclear weapon' Speaking in Alaska, Donald Trump is once again airing a list of familiar boasts and grievances, many of which are based on claims that are entirely untrue. Trump repeated his false claim that he had to start his war on Iran because, “they were two weeks away from having a nuclear weapon”. In fact, two months into Trump’s second term, US intelligence agencies reported to Congress in 2025 that Iran had suspended its pursuit of nuclear weapons in 2003. Despite that assessment, in the summer of 2025, Trump ordered the US bombing of Iran’s nuclear enrichment facilities which he later claimed had “obliterated” the country’s nuclear program. Eight months later, in February 2026, Trump announced that a full-scale war on Iran was necessary to stop Iran from obtaining nuclear weapons.
